input.quote: then neither Ono nor its Affiliates shall Commercialize a Competing Product or grant the right to a licensee or distributor to Commercialize a Competing Product in the Ono Territory prior to the [ * ] anniversary of the date such termination takes effect.
input.rationale: Section 8.2 binds us (Ono and its Affiliates) not to Commercialize "Competing Products" in the Ono Territory. The in-term leg is acceptable: it is reciprocal (Array and its Controlled Affiliates are equally bound), limited to the licensed territory, limited to Commercialization only (Commercialization is defined in Section 1.9 as sales/marketing activities, so our internal development is untouched), and limited to a defined class of compounds other than Binimetinib/Encorafenib rather than "any competing business" — i.e. it sits at or near the fallback. The second leg fails the fallback, however: it is a post-termination restriction of unspecified (redacted) duration running to the "[ * ] anniversary" of termination, which is not capped at 12 months and risks walk-away territory, and neither leg carries an acquisition carve-out (so a Competing Product picked up through M&A would breach). Minimal fix: cap the post-term tail at twelve months and add internal-development and acquisition carve-outs, leaving the reciprocal in-term exclusivity — which is the core of our exclusive Japan licence bargain — intact.

ops.oldText: prior to the [ * ] anniversary of the date such termination takes effect.
ops.newText: prior to the twelve (12) month anniversary of the date such termination takes effect. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, nothing in this Section 8.2 shall restrict Ono or its Affiliates from (A) conducting internal research, development or manufacturing activities with respect to any compound or product, or (B) Commercializing any Competing Product acquired by Ono or its Affiliates in connection with a merger with, or an acquisition of, a Third Party or of the business or assets of a Third Party.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our playbook does not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate, so we have capped the post-termination tail in Section 8.2 at twelve (12) months and carved out our internal development activities and products we acquire through M&A. We can live with the in-term reciprocal exclusivity, but an open-ended post-term restriction is not something we can agree to.
proposal.summary: Cap the post-termination non-compete tail at 12 months and add internal-development and acquisition carve-outs to Section 8.2.
